response.sql:
WITH currency_stats AS (
  SELECT
    feecoin,
    AVG(CASE WHEN rebtotal != 0 THEN rebtotal ELSE NULL END) AS avg_rebtotal,
    AVG(CASE WHEN rebrate != 0 AND feerate != 0 THEN (rebrate - feerate) / feerate ELSE NULL END) AS avg_gap
  FROM fees
  GROUP BY feecoin
),
benchmark_calc AS (
  SELECT
    AVG(avg_rebtotal) AS benchmark_value
  FROM currency_stats
),
filtered_currencies AS (
  SELECT
    cs.feecoin,
    cs.avg_rebtotal,
    cs.avg_gap
  FROM currency_stats cs
  WHERE cs.avg_rebtotal IS NOT NULL
    AND (SELECT benchmark_value FROM benchmark_calc) IS NOT NULL
    AND cs.avg_rebtotal > (SELECT benchmark_value FROM benchmark_calc)
)
SELECT
  (SELECT AVG(avg_rebtotal) FROM filtered_currencies) AS avg_of_avg_rebates,
  (SELECT AVG(avg_gap) FROM filtered_currencies) AS avg_of_avg_gaps,
  (SELECT AVG(avg_rebtotal) FROM filtered_currencies) - (SELECT benchmark_value FROM benchmark_calc) AS avg_excess_over_benchmark;

assumptions.assumption: Records with rebtotal = 0 are skipped from the rebate average (zero is treated as 'not applicable' rather than NULL), while the gap calculation skips any record where rebrate = 0 or feerate = 0.
NULL values in feecoin form a single currency group, as 'records lacking a currency forming one group'.
The query always returns exactly one row; if no currencies exceed the benchmark or the benchmark is NULL, the row contains all NULLs.

alternatives.interpretation: If 'skip a zero rebate' for the gap average means skip any record where rebrate is zero OR non-positive (rather than only zero), the gap CASE would be `WHEN rebrate > 0 AND feerate > 0`. This produces the same result when rebrate and feerate are non-negative quantities.
alternatives.sql: ...CASE WHEN rebrate > 0 AND feerate > 0 THEN (rebrate - feerate) / feerate ELSE NULL END...
